correctness.rationale: For all n>=7 the proof eliminates empty columns by cost k+2>=3 per maximal distance-two zero block; two disjoint endpoint pairs then force minimum n+2 and precisely two size-two columns. A singleton core of length >=3 must be a three-color rainbow period, giving six phases. Each flanking double has two choices and any outside endpoint singleton is forced. Each of the four profiles contributes 6*2*2=24 distinct valid sets, total 96. Direct brute graph enumeration n=2..7, a transfer DP n=1..200, and independently generated structures corroborate all tested instances.

value.rationale: Exact classification and constant multiplicity of all minimum two-dominating sets is a natural missing structural statistic for the simplest cyclic grid, whose minimum sizes are studied because of redundant resource placement. The four sharp boundary profiles and rigid three-periodicity explain a surprising n-independent optimizer count. It is not a textbook restatement of known minimum-size formulas.
